rationale: Extensive examination of all available literature on MAU2-related Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS7, OMIM #621570) supports the hypothesis. MAU2 was initially linked to CdLS in single-case reports (Parenti et al., 2020; Peng et al., 2024), and the largest cohort assembled to date describes only 18 individuals carrying 15 distinct heterozygous variants (Parenti et al., 2025/2026). Published individuals display a broad spectrum ranging from mild CdLS features to classic presentations, primarily featuring microcephaly and short stature without substantial sex-skewed penetrance or clear deterministic genotype-phenotype boundaries, though truncating variants cause haploinsufficiency and in-frame variants selectively disrupt NIPBL dimerization.

evidence.text: Parenti et al. (2025/2026) report the largest international cohort of MAU2-related CdLS to date, describing 18 individuals harboring 15 heterozygous variants (including both in-frame and truncating variants) with presentations ranging from classic CdLS to milder neurodevelopmental phenotypes.

source.title: Pathogenic variants in the cohesin loader subunit MAU2 lead to a new Cornelia de Lange Syndrome subtype
source.quote: We describe 18 individuals carrying 15 heterozygous MAU2 variants and demonstrate pathogenicity through functional analyses. MAU2 in-frame variants predominantly impair NIPBL–MAU2 interaction, whereas truncating variants cause MAU2 haploinsufficiency and lead to NIPBL reduction... Affected individuals display a wide range of phenotypes, from classic CdLS to milder presentations, with short stature and microcephaly as consistent features.

evidence.text: Parenti et al. (2020) initially identified MAU2 as a causative gene for CdLS through an isolated individual carrying a heterozygous in-frame deletion of 7 amino acids, confirming the scarcity of reported cases prior to recent series.

source.title: MAU2 and NIPBL variants impair the heterodimerization of the cohesin loader subunits and cause Cornelia de Lange syndrome
source.quote: Here we report a MAU2 variant causing CdLS, a deletion of seven amino acids that impairs the interaction between MAU2 and the NIPBL N terminus.

evidence.text: Peng et al. (2024) describe an individual with a novel missense variant in MAU2 (p.Arg176Trp) exhibiting core CdLS features, emphasizing that by late 2023 only a single individual had been previously documented in literature.

source.title: Clinical study and genetic analysis of Cornelia de Lange syndrome caused by a novel MAU2 gene variant in a Chinese boy
source.quote: Recent research has reported that loss-of-function variants affecting MAU2, which encodes a regulator of the cohesin complex, can cause CdLS. Thus far, only one MAU2-CdLS case has been reported worldwide. We detected a novel variant in MAU2 gene, NM_015329, c.526C>T (p.Arg176Trp) in a Chinese patient with CdLS

evidence.text: GeneReviews summary on Cornelia de Lange Syndrome recognizes MAU2 as an established causative locus alongside classical cohesin components, noting marked clinical variability spanning mild to classic presentations across non-NIPBL cohesinopathies.

source.title: Cornelia de Lange Syndrome - GeneReviews - NCBI - NIH
source.quote: The diagnosis of CdLS is established in a proband with suggestive clinical features and/or a heterozygous pathogenic variant in BRD4, MAU2, NIPBL, RAD21, or SMC3 or a hemizygous or heterozygous pathogenic variant in HDAC8 or SMC1A identified by molecular genetic testing.

new_directions.question_text: Do the two MAU2-specific episignature profiles correlate reliably with specific clinical severities or organ malformations in MAU2-CdLS?
new_directions.rationale: Parenti et al. identified two distinct MAU2 DNA methylation episignatures corresponding to truncating versus in-frame variants, but whether these molecular subsignatures stratify cognitive prognosis, structural heart disease, or limb reduction defects remains uncharacterized.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true prevalence of MAU2 missense variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in unexplained mild neurodevelopmental cohorts lacking classical CdLS craniofacial features?
new_directions.rationale: Because truncating and in-frame MAU2 variants frequently produce milder phenotypes that fail classical consensus diagnostic criteria, targeted re-analysis of whole-exome/genome sequencing data may identify non-syndromic neurodevelopmental cohorts harboring pathogenic MAU2 variants.
